custom.cols <- sample(c("red", "black"),

Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â  size = nInd(H3N2),

scatter(dapc1, col = custom.cols)

messages.subject: [adegenet-forum] DAPC axes
messages.body_plain:
Hi Said,

DAPC is a PCA on which you do a discriminant analysis. So the PCA gives you PCs (axes) on which you apply a discriminant analysis (LDs axes). The basic plot of the DAPC is the result of the discriminant analyses on the PCs. Therefore the axes of the basic plot are LDs
Good luck

Cathy

messages.subject: [adegenet-forum] DAPC axes
messages.body_plain:
Dear Said,

both terminologies are correct: LDs are merely PCs of a discriminant
analysis. But as DAPC has 2 sets of PCs, one of the initial PCA, then one
for the follow-up discriminant analysis, LDs will be less ambiguous.

As for the scale on scatterplots of DAPC: it is disabled by default as not
usually used, but you can add a grid using grid = TRUE. See ?scatter.dapc
for further options.

Best
Thibaut
